caption:
Meta has bought Conductor, the startup whose Mac app lets one developer run several AI coding agents, like Claude Code and Codex, at the same time.
The team joins Meta Superintelligence Labs. The price was not disclosed.
Conductor's cloud service shuts down on November 20.

Would you trust a team of AI agents to write your code?

Source: TechCrunch, SiliconANGLE · Photos: Meta, SiliconANGLE, PYMNTS
threads_text: Meta just bought Conductor, the app that lets one developer run Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents side by side. So Meta now owns a tool built around its rivals' agents. Do you run more than one AI coding agent at once?

paragraphs.text: Meta has acquired Conductor, a startup whose app lets software developers run several AI coding agents at the same time. Axios first reported the deal on November 4, 2026, and Meta confirmed it to TechCrunch without sharing further details. The price and other terms were not disclosed.

Conductor's founder and chief executive, Charlie Holtz, announced the news in a post and a blog entry on the company's website. According to PYMNTS, he wrote that he will work with Nat Friedman and Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, at Meta Superintelligence Labs, and that the team has "big, crazy plans for the next interface." Wang replied to the post with a welcome.

Conductor does not build its own AI models or agents. Its Mac app gives each coding agent an isolated copy of a project, so several agents can work on separate parts of the code at once while the developer reviews and merges the results, SiliconANGLE and The Register reported. The agents come from other companies, including Anthropic's Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex and Cursor, and users pay for them through their own subscriptions.

The company also ran Conductor Cloud, a hosted service that runs agents in sandboxed virtual machines for hours at a time and lets users check on them from an iPhone app. Conductor's website says more than 100,000 people use the product, according to SiliconANGLE.

Meta engineers were already customers. When Conductor raised a $22 million Series A in March from Spark Capital and Matrix, it named Meta, Google and Spotify as companies with dozens of engineers on the product, SiliconANGLE reported. The company was founded in 2024 by Holtz and chief technology officer Jackson de Campos and launched its main product in the summer of 2025.

Conductor is winding down its products. New sign-ups and downloads have stopped, and paying Pro subscribers get their paid features at no cost for now. The cloud service becomes view-only on November 13 and shuts down on November 20, after which the company will begin deleting stored data. Users can export their data or move cloud workspaces to their own machines before then, and active subscribers will receive refunds, according to SiliconANGLE.

The Mac app will keep working for several more months. In early 2027 it will stop receiving new models and critical bug fixes. Holtz said the team will have something new for customers by early next year. Conductor also said it has never sold user data or used it to train models.

A Meta spokesperson told The Register that the deal will strengthen the company's AI tools for developers. People familiar with the deal told Axios that Meta expects the Conductor team to speed up work on its next generation of AI coding tools, SiliconANGLE reported. Meta released Muse Code, a terminal coding agent, in August, and launched its Muse Wonder frontier models in October, according to PYMNTS.

Rivals are making similar moves. On the same day, OpenAI said it plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, which makes developer storage tools, after earlier agreeing to buy Ona, which runs coding agents in cloud sandboxes. The Register noted that Anthropic bought developer tools company Stainless in May. Meta's earlier 2026 deals, including the agent social network Moltbook, were smaller in scope, the publication said.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the deal shows where the competition in AI coding is moving. The models are only part of the product; the tools that let one developer supervise many agents at once are becoming just as valuable. Buying a tool that its own engineers already used gives Meta a team that has worked with the leading agents from its competitors.
The next thing to watch is the new interface Holtz promised for early 2027, and whether it is built around Meta's Muse Code and Muse models or keeps supporting agents from Anthropic and OpenAI.
